latin: Potest anima per extrinsecam informationem ad hoc deuenire, ut omnia per substantialem suam formam indiuisibiliter intelligat.
translation: The soul can come, by an extrinsic informing, to the point where it understands all things indivisibly through its own substantial form.
translation_note: 'Indiuisibiliter': the mode of understanding proper to a substantial form, not the discursive, divisible mode of ordinary cognition; Farmer's note groups this thesis with the surrounding cluster as central to Pico's theory of knowledge (farmer1998:21288).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch14, from Latin at farmer1998:21278
attribution: Among the conclusions Pico titles 'paradoxical, according to his own opinion, introducing new teachings in philosophy' (kabbalah_paradigma:1324).
doctrine: The thesis holds that the soul, informed from outside itself, can come to understand all things at once and indivisibly through its own substantial form, rather than piecemeal (farmer1998:21278); Farmer's apparatus cross-references it to 3>60, 'Nihil intelligit actu et distincte anima, nisi se ipsam' [the soul understands nothing actually and distinctly, except itself] (farmer1998:21254).
historiography: Farmer's own note describes this thesis, with its neighbors, as among the key propositions of Pico's theory of knowledge, and points to a fuller discussion elsewhere in his book without giving its content here (farmer1998:21288); an unauthored German-language study cites it together with 3>60, 3>61, and 3>52 as a further group bearing on self-knowledge and the unity of the sciences (kabbalah_paradigma:1695).
not_established: The content of Farmer's fuller discussion referenced at farmer1998:21288 is not given in the material consulted.
